title: Collinear and noncollinear antiferromagnetic ordering in a highly frustrated decorated square kagomé lattice antiferromagnets of the nabokoite family
authors: V. N. Glazkov, Ya V. Rebrov, M. A. Dubovitskii, M. M. Markina, K. V. Zakharov, A. F. Murtazoev, P. S. Berdonosov, A. N. Vasiliev
abstract: Nabokoite family compounds ACu$_7$(TeO$_4$)(SO4)$_5$X (A=Na, K, Rb, Cs; X=Cl, Br) host frustrated 2D square kagom'{e} lattice layers decorated by additional inter-layer magnetic ions. We study magnetic order in nabokoites with multi-frequency electron spin resonance spectroscopy and thermodynamic measurement (specific heat, magnetization and dielectric permittivity). Our study reveals that the choice of the low-temperature ground state is qualitatively different in light-alkali-ion (K, Na) and heavy-alkali-ion (Rb, Cs) compounds. Heavy-alkali-ion nabokoites order in conventional collinear antiferromagnetic pattern with easy-axis anisotropy. The parameters of the ordered antiferromagnetic state are very close for all heavy-alkali-ion subfamily. Light-alkali-ion members of nabokoite family demonstrate much more complicated route to the ordered state: firstly, a ferroelectric transition at 25-90K lifts the frustration and thus pre-cooks the low-temperature ordering; secondly, an unusual noncollinear magnetic order develops via two-step phase transition with first transition temperature $T_{c1}\simeq 5-6$K and the second transition at $T_{c2}\simeq 3-4$K. Noncollinear order is evidenced by observation of characteristic non-Larmor antiferromagnetic resonance mode. Spin dynamics of light-alkali-ion nabokoites is characterized by three zero-field magnon gaps and two spin-reorientation fields, the values of magnon gaps and critical fields are quite different for different compounds. The finite-size cluster modeling of pyramidal structural block of nabokoite structure combined suggests that the critical closeness of the nabokoite exchange coupling parameters to the border-line between the different quantum ground state of pyramidal building block of nabokoite structure could be the clue to the choice of qualitatively different ordered state in light- and heavy-alkali-ion nabokoites.
summary: This paper investigates the magnetic ordering in frustrated nabokoite compounds, finding a qualitative difference in the ground state based on the alkali metal ion used. By combining ESR, thermodynamics, and structural analysis, the authors distinguish between conventional collinear and complex noncollinear magnetic patterns. The work highlights how subtle changes in chemical composition can fundamentally alter the magnetic quantum ground state of these frustrated materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the nature of magnetic ordering (collinear vs. noncollinear) in highly frustrated antiferromagnets.
main_result: The magnetic ordering pattern in nabokoite compounds is qualitatively different depending on whether light- or heavy-alkali-ions are present, suggesting the structural/electronic environment dictates the ground state.
method: The research combines multi-frequency electron spin resonance spectroscopy, thermodynamic measurements (specific heat, magnetization), and finite-size cluster modeling.
model_or_system: The system is the nabokoite family of compounds, $	ext{ACu}_7(	ext{TeO}_4)(	ext{SO}_4)_5	ext{X}$, which feature frustrated 2D square kagomé lattice layers.
key_observables: Antiferromagnetic resonance modes, specific heat anomalies, magnetization curves, and dielectric permittivity transitions.
important_parameters: The choice of alkali ion (light vs. heavy) and the critical closeness of exchange coupling parameters to quantum ground state boundaries.
main_assumptions: The choice of ordering pattern is hypothesized to be pre-determined by high-temperature dielectric transitions, and modeling relies on averaging over random powder orientations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate crystal structure, lattice constant ratios, and show characteristic AFMR patterns and specific heat/dielectric anomalies marking phase transitions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares magnetic behavior across different alkali-ion subfamilies, using multiple experimental techniques to characterize the transition from frustrated states to either collinear or noncollinear magnetic order.
why_interesting: The interplay between structural transitions (ferroelectric) and magnetic ordering in frustrated lattices provides a rich platform for studying quantum phase transitions and emergent magnetic ground states.

FIG. 2. (color online) Low-temperature specific heat curves Cp(T) for nabokoite family compounds ACu7(TeO4)(SO4)5X (A=Na, K, Cs, Rb; X=Cl, Br). Left panel: light-alkali- ion nabokoites (A=Na, K). Right panel: heavy-alkali-ion nabokoites (A=Rb, Cs). Vertical arrows marks positions of specific heat peaks corresponding to the low-temperature phase transitions (see Table I). Dashed and dash-dotted lines correspond to T 3 and T 2 dependences expected for 3D and 2D Heisenberg antiferromagnets, correspondingly.

FIG. 4. (color online) Temperature evolution of the elec- tron spin resonance absorption in the powder sample of RbCu7(TeO4)(SO4)5Br at f = 34.0 GHz. Dashed curve close to the 7.0 K absorption spectrum is a Lorentzian fit of the ESR absorption line above the N´eel point, curve is shifted for clar- ity. Horizontal dashed line over the 4.5 K absorption shows “no absorption” level to highlight broad absorption band at low fields appearing below the N´eel point. Narrow absorption signal at 1.0...1.2 T is a paramagnetic resonance response from a small amount (about 1% per copper ion of nabokoite) of free paramagnetic centers [24].

Sample is placed in the geometrical center of the rectangular microwave cavity, “(electr.)” and “(magn.)” notes mark experiments with the sample positioned in the maximum of microwave electric and magnetic field correspondingly.
